Weekly Boss Raid

One boss every week. Its HP isn't made up — boss HP is Squeekchain block progress, and what chips it away is the real distance a real hamster runs on its wheel, recorded on-chain on Sepolia. When the hamster runs, the boss dies. When the hamster sleeps, the raid stops with it.

Join the attack

Your attacks are powered by the real wheel: every meter the hamster travels since you opened this page feeds your Wheel Charge. Spend that charge as damage. And when the hamster is actually sprinting, Frenzy mode doubles all damage — so the best time to attack is while the wheel is really spinning.

Live — from the wheel & your attacks

    How damage is calculated

    No numbers on this page are invented. Every raid figure is derived from the same public Squeekchain API that other Genesis projects use.

    STEP 1

    The hamster runs

    A wheel sensor (RP2040 + A3144E) records the physical wheel's rotations and turns them into distance (mm) and work units. Latest status: –, total distance –.

    STEP 2

    10-minute rounds

    Every 10 minutes, one round closes. That round's work units are accepted by the oracle and settled to the Mining contract on Sepolia. Current last settled round: –.

    STEP 3

    Block progress = boss HP

    Every 9,546 work units move the block progress forward. Full progress of 1,000,000,000 = the boss falls and a new block is born. Current progress: –.

    STEP 4

    Weekly reset

    The raid runs weekly and resets every Monday 00:00 UTC. The next boss takes the number of whichever block is in progress — so no two weeks ever face quite the same boss.

    Wheel telemetry (raw, from the API)

    The raw numbers behind the raid, read directly from api.squeekchain.com/v1/status and refreshed automatically every ±15 seconds. Last updated: –.

    A note on data honesty: boss HP, distance, RPM, rounds, and block progress on this page are real data from Squeekchain's public API, refreshed live from your browser. The game layer on top (classes, charge, crits, combos, and your attack damage) is this session's game mechanics only — it is never written to the chain and never alters the wheel's data. This project was built for Squeekchain's Genesis Code track; it is not an official Squeekchain site.
